scores.rationale: Worn Australian tea tins and sacks, Launceston Crown Mills sack adds local interest; roughly $30-80 as a group.
Likely Yamaha student alto with case and stand, but model and playability unconfirmed and used market is soft; about $200-400.
Pencil-signed Pro Hart print has uncertain authenticity and value; Lindsay giclees are publisher-signed reproductions worth little.
Nine Will Young Widecombe figures at modest prices each plus a print, one broken; about $60-100 in total.
Attribution unconfirmed with no backstamp; decorative Memphis style porcelain tea set worth about $50-100.
Probable McHugh Launceston 3 gallon crock with worn stamp, local collector demand, about $80-150 with stool.
Large primitive painted cupboard with borer and damage; decorator interest, realistic $100-250.
Copper timpani shell with no head or hoop, dented; mainly decorative, about $40-80.
Common Hohner single-row accordion, torn bellows and missing keys; decorative only, under $30-40.
1930s Royal De Luxe portable with case and papers is common; worn, about $50-90.
